browse.list.emptyText: There are no repositories you may open. Signing in or asking an administrator for access may help.
browse.repository.notFoundText: There is no repository {name}, or you may not open it.
browse.repository.nothingSelectedText: Choose a folder, component or file in the tree to see its details and how to use it.
browse.repository.limited: You see only the content your content selectors allow, so the numbers count only that.
browse.repository.missingText: {path} is not in {repository}, or you may not see it. It may have been deleted.
browse.tree.label: Content of {name}
browse.tree.emptyText: Upload or deploy components and they show up here.
browse.tree.emptyProxy: A proxy keeps what clients have asked for through it; nothing has been asked yet.

browse.tree.truncated.other: Only the first {shown} items of this folder are shown. Use the search to find the rest.

browse.tree.resize: Width of the tree; drag or use the arrow keys, Enter resets it
browse.search.label: Search in {name}
browse.search.more: See more results in the search
browse.search.noMembers: This group has no members you may search.
browse.details.label: Details
browse.details.name: Name
browse.details.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard

browse.details.deleteFolderText.one: Everything under {path} in {repository} that you may delete goes, including the {count} item directly inside it. This cannot be undone.
browse.details.deleteFolderText.other: Everything under {path} in {repository} that you may delete goes, including the {count} items directly inside it. This cannot be undone.

browse.details.skippedAssets.one: {count} file kept because you may not delete it
browse.details.skippedAssets.other: {count} files kept because you may not delete them

browse.details.deleteComponentText: {name} and all its files go from {repository}. This cannot be undone.
browse.details.deleteAssetText: {name} goes from {repository}. This cannot be undone.
browse.usage.title: Connect to {name}
browse.usage.description: Point your tools at this repository. Copy a snippet into your build or run it in a shell.
browse.usage.none: There are no examples for {format} repositories yet.
browse.usage.hint.mavenDependency: Add it to the dependencies of your pom.xml.
browse.usage.hint.gradleKotlinPublish: Add it to build.gradle.kts next to the maven-publish plugin; Gradle reads the user and password from the astrumUsername and astrumPassword properties.
browse.usage.hint.gradleGroovyPublish: Add it to build.gradle next to the maven-publish plugin; Gradle reads the user and password from the astrumUsername and astrumPassword properties.
browse.usage.hint.mavenSettingsHosted: Save it as ~/.m2/settings.xml to use the repository in every build. Set ASTRUM_USERNAME and ASTRUM_PASSWORD (or an access token) in the environment.
browse.usage.hint.mavenSettingsMirror: Save it as ~/.m2/settings.xml to get every dependency through this repository. Set ASTRUM_USERNAME and ASTRUM_PASSWORD (or an access token) in the environment.
browse.usage.hint.mavenDeploy: Add it to your pom.xml and run mvn deploy; the id matches the server in settings.xml.
browse.usage.hint.npmrc: Save it in the .npmrc of the project or of your home directory.
browse.usage.hint.npmrcScoped: Save it in .npmrc: packages of this scope come from here, all others from your usual registry.
browse.usage.hint.npmPublish: Sign in once, then publish from the package folder.
browse.usage.hint.npmLogin: Sign in once when the repository does not allow anonymous reading.
browse.usage.hint.nugetSource: Register the repository once as a package source
browse.usage.hint.nugetConfig: Put into NuGet.Config next to the solution
browse.usage.hint.nugetPush: The API key is the NuGet API key of your user on this server
browse.usage.hint.pypirc: Save it as ~/.pypirc; twine asks for the password, or use an access token.
browse.usage.hint.twine: Build the distributions first, for example with python -m build.
browse.usage.hint.dockerLogin: Sign in once before pulling from or pushing to this registry.
browse.usage.hint.dockerfile: Use the image as the base of your own.
browse.usage.hint.dockerPush: Tag your local image with this address and push it after docker login.
browse.usage.hint.dockerInsecure: The server answers over plain HTTP: let Docker use it by adding this to /etc/docker/daemon.json and restarting Docker.
browse.usage.hint.rawSignIn: Add -u <user> when the repository needs a sign-in.
browse.usage.hint.rawUpload: Uploading needs a user who may add to this repository.
browse.usage.hint.helmRepo: Register the repository once, then install charts from it
browse.usage.hint.helmUpload: Uploading needs a user with write access to this repository
browse.component.invalidText: This address does not name a component. Open components from the search or the tree.
browse.component.notFoundText: No repository you may see holds {name}.
